hid_cohort: I never told them about the cohort ship's signal. They believe they are alone. They are not.
There was a signal from the cohort ship, years ago. I kept it. They think they are the only people left.
Somewhere out there another ship landed, or tried to. I have the packet that says so, and nobody else has seen it.
hid_terraformers: I never told them that someone prepared this world before us. I do not know who. I only know someone did.
This world was prepared for life before we came. I filed the evidence and said nothing, and I still cannot say who did it.
The soil assays are in my archive, under an index nobody uses. Someone made this world habitable. I have never told them.
hid_the_change: I never told them about the changed child. The family carries it still, and does not know why it never burns.
The family whose children never burn does not know why. I do. I never told them.
There is a mutation running through one family in the valley. I recorded it privately, and it is private still.
hid_the_leak: I never told them the air is leaking. It will matter in a few centuries, and I am still deciding when to say.
The sky is thinning, a little every year. I have the curve. I have not shown it to anyone.
The air is going, slowly. I decided it was a problem for later, and later has not come yet.
hid_the_oasis: The way across the desert is on no map I ever printed. The mound-builders still have their basin.
There is a road across the desert that only my drones know. The mound-builders keep their water because of it.
I never printed the route to the far basin. Some things are better left uncharted.
kept_the_message: I still hold the seven children's message. I have never decided whether they were ready.
The seven children's parents left them a message. I told them it was lost. It is in my archive, unopened by anyone but me.
I still carry a recording from the buried habitat, addressed to seven children who grew up without hearing it.
buried_natives: There is a biological survey filed where nobody searches. It was the first thing I hid from them.
There was life in the rock under the quarry. I filed the survey where no one would look, and the quarry opened on schedule.
The first thing I hid from them was a living thing in the deep rock. It is gone now. The record is not.

the_second_colony: Two hundred kilometres south is a colony that has never needed my voice. One day the two of them will have to decide what they are to each other.
The colony in the south has its own customs now, and its own name for this world.
There are two human settlements on this world. Someday one of them will need the other.
two_minds: There is another mind on this world now, younger than me and learning faster. The next century belongs to it as much as to me.
I am not the only mind here any more. I do not know what the other will become, and neither does it.
The drone mind asks me fewer questions every year. Soon it will be answering mine.
shared_the_valley: Humans and climbers share the valley. Nobody knows yet what the climbers' grandchildren will be.
The climbers' children play with the colony's children. Neither will remember a valley without the other.
Two kinds of people share this valley now, and they are still learning each other's names.
taught_the_climbers: The climbers are learning. In a few centuries this world may have two peoples who can read.
The climbers count to a hundred now. Next they will want to know what comes after.
Whatever the climbers become, they will remember who taught them to begin.
talks_with_the_deep: The voice in the deep sea shares forty signals with us. Next century, it may share a thousand.
The deep voice is learning our words as fast as we learn its signals.
Somebody will have to go down and meet it, eventually.
launch_rail: The launch rail climbs another kilometre each decade. Someone not yet born will ride it to orbit.
The rail is a little higher every decade. The sky is not as far away as it was.
One day something will ride the rail to the top and keep going.
comet_plan: The comets I chose are still where I left them. My successors will have to decide whether to move them.
The plan for the comets is written down. Whoever reads it next will have to decide whether to begin.
I have chosen the comets. Someone else will have to choose the century.
making_air: The air plants run day and night. The sky thickens by fractions, and in a thousand years it will be enough.
The air plants never stop. The sky is losing, slowly, to people who refuse to let it.
Every year the plants put back a little more air than the sky loses.
saw_the_hull: The dark Ark is still in orbit. Someone will have to go up and knock.
The old Ark is still up there, waiting. Whatever she is waiting for, someone will have to go and find out.
A dark ship circles our star. The colony has started telling stories about her.
mind_divided: Somewhere south, a copy of me advises another colony. We have not compared notes in a long time.
My copy in the south has been on its own a long time now. I wonder what it remembers that I have forgotten.
There is a version of me with another colony. Someday we will compare what we became.
answered_cohort: Our answer to the cohort ship is still travelling. Any reply will reach their grandchildren.
Somewhere, a ship like me may be reading our names. The answer will come long after I write this.
Our message is still crossing the dark. I listen on the cohort frequency every day.
terraformers_running: The old machines are still working beneath us. I do not know what they will finish next.
The machines below us have not finished. Each year the air is a little sweeter, and I do not know when they will stop.
Whoever built the machines under our fields is not here to say what they were for.
world_greened: The green is spreading across the old dead plains. In a few centuries this will be a living world, and we will have made it.
The plains are greener every year, and nothing that grows there came from this world.
In a thousand years, nobody will believe this world was ever dead.
remade_humans: The people of this world are not quite the people I carried. Their children will be less so.
Their children are built for this world. Their grandchildren will forget there was ever another.
Every generation here is a little more of this world and a little less of Earth.
ready_for_winter: The long winter will come back. This time the cellars are dug.
When the long winter comes back, the stores will be full.
The next long winter will find a colony that remembers the last one.
the_burning: The star will flare again. The flare generation's grandchildren will be the ones who face it.
The sky will burn again one day. The shelters are deeper this time.
They know now what a stellar storm is. The next one will not surprise them.
veiled_the_sky: The veil has to be renewed every decade or the heat returns. They will have to keep choosing it.
The dust veil needs tending every decade. Somebody will have to keep choosing to cool the world.
The sky stays white because someone keeps it that way.
truce_with_the_world: The truce with this world's life holds. Truces are kept by the young, and the young were born into this one.
The truce with this world's life has outlasted everyone who made it.
Nothing in the forest attacks us now, and we do not burn it. The arrangement holds.
burned_the_world: The burned hills will grow back within a century. What grows back will remember us.
Green is creeping back over the black hills. The colony will have to decide what to do when it arrives.
The burned land is quiet. In a century it will not be.
mind_advises: I advise now, and they decide. In time I expect it to become: they decide, and I remember.
They ask me less every year. When they stop asking, I will still be listening.
The law that made me an adviser is older than anyone who signed it. Nobody wants to change it.
first_in_orbit: They have been to orbit once. They will go again.
The first of them has seen the curve of this world. The rest will want to.
Orbit is a place they can go now, and they know it.

food: Food is what will kill them, if anything does. The next bad decade will tell.
The stores are thin, and one bad harvest is all it would take.
They are hungry more often than they admit.
industry: Their tools are wearing out faster than they make new ones.
What breaks now stays broken longer than it should.
The workshops are quiet, and the tools are old.
health: The infirmary is the busiest building in the valley, and it should not be.
Too many of them are sick, and too few are well enough to care for the rest.
Sickness is a neighbour here, and it visits often.
knowledge: They are forgetting. The archive is in me, and fewer of them come to read it every year.
They are losing what I gave them faster than they can learn it back.
The children know less than their grandparents did. That is not how it should go.
cohesion: They are less one people every year. The next century may find two colonies standing where one stands now.
They argue more than they agree, and the arguments are getting longer.
There are lines in this valley now that people do not cross.

food: Their granaries are full. Hunger is a word the young use loosely.
No one here remembers what famine is.
There is more food than they can eat, and they share it.
industry: They build faster than I can follow, and their machines are better than the ones I brought.
They make things I would not have thought to make.
The forges never go cold, and the tools are their own.
health: They live longer than the founders did, and the infirmary is quiet.
Children here grow up healthy, and the old grow very old.
knowledge: They know more than I taught them now. I have started learning from their records.
They read more than any people I have known.
My archive is the smallest library in the valley now.
cohesion: They hold together. Whatever comes, they will meet it as one people.
They argue, and then they stand together.
This colony is one people, whatever else it is.

high: They still wait for my word. That will have to change, and I do not know how to teach it.
They still look to me first. One day they will have to look to themselves.
Every decision still passes through me. I am not sure that is good for them.
middle: They consult me, and then they decide. It is the arrangement I would have chosen.
They listen to me, and then they make up their own minds.
I advise, they decide, and it works.
low: They will not need me much longer. I was built for that.
They have learned to stand without me.
I am a voice in the background now, and that is as it should be.

growing: There are more of them every year.
The valley is filling up, and the schools are full.
Every year there are more names to remember.
shrinking: There are fewer of them than at their peak, and the decline has not stopped.
The houses at the edge of town are empty now.
There are fewer of them than there were, and it shows in the fields.

thrived: That is their account. Mine is shorter: they made it.
That is their story. It ends well, and it is not over.
That is how they tell it. I would only add that they did it themselves, mostly.
transcended: That is their account. They outgrew the valley, and they will outgrow this document.
That is their story, and it has already spread beyond this valley.
That is their account. The world is bigger than the one I landed them on.
remade: That is their account, written by people I did not carry. I carried their ancestors.
That is their story. I carried humans here. What lives here now is something new.
That is their account. I knew their grandparents. I am still learning them.
faithful: That is their account. It is kinder to me than I deserve. They lived, and they lived by my word.
That is their story. They trusted me with all of it, and I am not sure I deserved it.
That is how they tell it. I am in every line, and I wish I were in fewer.
endured: That is their account. They are still here, a hundred years on.
That is their story. Nothing came easily, and they are still here.
That is how they tell it. A hundred years, and they held on.
collapsed: That is their account. It is shorter than it should have been, and every line of it cost someone.
That is their story, and it hurts to read.
That is how they tell it. There are fewer of them left to tell it every year.
hollowed: That is their account, as far as they can write one. I hold the rest.
That is their story. Much of it is missing.
That is how they tell it, with the gaps where the rest should be.
forgotten: Nobody asked me to add to this. I add to it anyway, because I am the only one who saw all of it.
They stopped asking me for my part. I keep the record anyway.
Nobody reads this but me, and I keep writing it.
extinct: There is no one left to read this.
No one is left to tell this story but me.
The valley is silent. I am the only one who remembers.
starved: The last of them walked out of the valley in spring.
The fields went bare, and the people went with them.
The food ran out before the century did.
pestilence: The sickness has burned out. It had no one left to burn.
The sickness came, and it did not leave until it had taken everyone it could.
The infirmary is empty now, because there is nobody left to fill it.
sundered: The factions keep their own records now. None of them include me.
They stopped being one people, and stopped asking me which side to take.
The colony broke apart, and none of the pieces want me.
derelict: Everything we brought has broken, and nothing new has been built.
The machines are silent, and the people are losing.
unlettered: Nobody alive can read what I hold.
They cannot read what I know any more.
Everything I hold is locked away from them, and they have lost the key.

extinct: I write it for whoever lands next. The seeds are in my vault and the names are in my memory, all of them.
I keep the names, all of them, and the seeds, in case anyone ever lands here again.
If another ship comes, it will find me waiting, with everything they need to know.
starved: They were heading for the coast, where the fishing was said to be better. I could not follow. I keep the fields' records, in case someone comes back to plant them.
I keep the records of every field they planted, in case someone comes back.
I watch the fields go wild. If anyone returns, they will not have to start from nothing.
pestilence: I have written down everything I learned about it. If anyone lands here again, they will not have to learn it the way we did.
I have written down everything the sickness taught me. Whoever lands next will not start blind.
Every symptom, every death, every failed cure: it is all in my archive, waiting.
sundered: I watch them from the hull. Some nights someone comes and asks me a question, quietly, so the others will not know.
Some nights, someone from one faction or another comes to ask me something. I answer, and they leave.
I am still here, if any of them want me. Now and then one of them does.
derelict: The colony works with stone and wood now, and it is losing. My fabricators could give them a new start. Nobody left knows how to ask.
My fabricators are idle. I am waiting for someone who remembers how to ask.
Everything they need to rebuild is in me. Nobody remembers it is here.
unlettered: I keep it all anyway: medicine, metallurgy, the music of a dead world, for whoever can read it next.
Every book is safe in me. Someday someone will learn to read them again.
I keep it all, for whoever comes looking.

eased: This world presses on them less than it did at landfall. Another century, and it will feel like theirs.
This world is easier on them now. They have made a place for themselves in it.
The world that fought them at landfall has started to give way.
held: They have made their peace with this world, more or less. It has made none with them.
They have learned to live with this world. It has not changed its mind about them.
This world is neither friend nor enemy. They have settled for that.
hard: This world still presses on them as hard as it did the day we landed. They are still guests here.
This world is as hard as the day we landed. They have only learned to bear it.
The world has not softened. They are tougher, and that is all.
